#include <stdio.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "cholesky.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++) {
    if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		     DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;


#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     //j<i
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
           A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
        }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
     }
     // i==j case
     for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
        A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
     }
     A[i][i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i][i]);
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_cholesky (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-01 ---
domain:
    # Full logical domain; triangular structure is expressed in the computation via j < i, k < j.
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A is an N×N matrix stored in row-major layout.
    # Only the lower-triangular part (j <= i) is used/updated by the kernel.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    # Tunable constants for performance; values should be chosen based on cache sizes and SIMD width.
    T_I: int  # tile size for i (e.g., 64)
    T_J: int  # tile size for j within each row (e.g., 64)
    T_K: int  # tile size for k in reductions (e.g., 64)
    V_K: int  # SIMD vector width along k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky factorization: A becomes its own lower-triangular factor L.
    for i in seq(0, N):
        # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # dot_ij = Σ_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                DOT_OFF:
                    dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # A[i, j] ← (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                OFF:
                    A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal element in row i.
        # dot_ii = Σ_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[i, k]
        DOT_DIAG:
            dot_ii = sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        # A[i, i] ← sqrt(A[i, i] - dot_ii)
        # SQRT_FUN in the original code is modeled as the standard sqrt for DATA_TYPE.
        DIAG:
            A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - dot_ii)

dependencies:
    # Within a fixed row i, the off-diagonal elements A[i, j] must be computed left-to-right
    # because A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for all k < j that were produced by earlier OFF updates.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):
        OFF(i, j-1) -> OFF(i, j)

    # The diagonal element A[i, i] depends on all off-diagonal elements of row i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        OFF(i, j) -> DIAG(i)

    # The outer loop over i is strictly sequential (left-looking factorization):
    # row i depends on all rows 0..i-1 having been fully factorized.
    # This is already enforced by "for i in seq(0, N)" but is stated explicitly here.
    for i in [1, N):
        DIAG(i-1) -> OFF(i, 0)

optimization:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Blocking / tiling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block the outer i-loop to improve temporal locality for rows of A.
    # This preserves the sequential order of i within each tile, so the
    # Cholesky row-to-row dependencies remain intact.
    block(i, I, T_I)

    # Block the j-loop within each row i. Although j’s upper bound depends
    # on i (j < i), the blocking is applied over the full [0, N) range,
    # with the j < i condition still guarding the triangular region.
    # This improves reuse when processing bands of the lower triangle.
    block(j, J, T_J)

    # Block the k-dimension of the dot products so that each k-tile fits
    # into L1/L2 cache. This reduces cache misses when streaming A[i, k]
    # and A[j, k] in the reductions.
    block(k, K, T_K)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost k-iteration in both dot products:
    #   dot_ij = Σ A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #   dot_ii = Σ A[i, k] * A[i, k]
    # Mapping these to SIMD FMA instructions significantly increases throughput.
    vectorize(k, V_K)

    # Additional unrolling of k increases ILP (instruction-level parallelism)
    # and helps hide the latency of loads and floating-point operations.
    unroll(k, 4)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelism
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The outer i-loop and the j-loop inside a row cannot be parallelized
    # due to true data dependencies (each row depends on all previous rows,
    # and each A[i, j] depends on A[i, k] for k < j).
    #
    # However, the reductions over k for a fixed (i, j) are mathematically
    # associative, so they can be parallelized across k-tiles K. Each
    # thread computes a partial sum over a subset of K and partial sums
    # are combined at the end of the reduction.
    parallelize(K)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar replacement / register promotion (conceptual)
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The compiler is encouraged to keep frequently used scalar values,
    # such as A[j, j] and the running sums dot_ij, dot_ii, in registers.
    # This is implied by the formulation using scalar temporaries (dot_ij,
    # dot_ii) and the absence of aliasing, and does not require an
    # explicit directive in this model.
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-02 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Full N×N matrix stored row-major; only the lower triangle (j ≤ i) is used.
    # On input: A is symmetric positive definite.
    # On output: A holds the Cholesky factor L (lower-triangular) such that A ≈ L · Lᵀ.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    N: int  # matrix dimension

    # Cache / SIMD tuning parameters
    TI: int  # tile size for i (e.g., 32)
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    TK: int  # tile size for k-reductions (e.g., 64)
    V:  int  # SIMD width for vectorization over k (e.g., 8 for AVX-512 double)

computation:
    # Off-diagonal entries: for each row i, columns j < i.
    # This expresses the left-looking Cholesky update:
    #   A[i,j] = (A[i,j] - ∑_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[j,k]) / A[j,j]
    # written in one assignment so that the sum is accumulated in registers
    # instead of repeatedly updating A[i,j] in memory.
    OFFDIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            for j in seq([0, i)):   # sequential in j: A[i,j] depends on A[i,0..j-1]
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    / A[j, j]

    # Diagonal entries:
    #   A[i,i] = sqrt( A[i,i] - ∑_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k]^2 )
    # again with the reduction written explicitly.
    DIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

dependencies:
    # Within a fixed row i, off-diagonal elements must be computed in increasing j,
    # because A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for all k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, N), j2 in [0, N):
        if (j1 < j2) and (j2 < i):
            OFFDIAG(i, j1) -> OFFDIAG(i, j2)

    # Each off-diagonal element A[i,j] depends on the entire row j (0..j) being
    # already factorized, in particular on A[j,j] (for the division) and
    # A[j,k] for k < j (used in the dot product).
    # This is enforced by depending on DIAG(j), which in turn depends on all
    # OFFDIAG(j, k) with k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        if j < i:
            DIAG(j) -> OFFDIAG(i, j)

    # The diagonal element A[i,i] depends on all off-diagonal elements in row i,
    # since its reduction uses A[i,k] for k < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        if j < i:
            OFFDIAG(i, j) -> DIAG(i)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------
    # Loop blocking (tiling)
    # ------------------------------

    # Block the outer i and j dimensions. This restructures the triangular
    # iteration into tiles but preserves the original lexicographic order
    # (and thus dependencies). Many tiles will be partially filled because
    # of the j < i constraint, but data locality improves: elements of nearby
    # rows/columns live in cache together.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)
    hoist(I)   # I is the outermost loop
    hoist(J)   # J is just inside I, before the scalar i,j loops

    # Block the reduction dimension k for both reductions. This lets us:
    #   - operate on TK-sized chunks of rows A[i,*] and A[j,*],
    #   - keep those chunks in cache,
    #   - vectorize efficiently across k.
    # The transformation logically turns
    #   sum(k in [0, bound)) ...
    # into nested sums over tiles Kb and intra-tile k, handling short
    # last tiles when bound is not multiple of TK.
    block(k, Kb, TK)
    hoist(Kb)  # Kb is hoisted outside the innermost loops to reuse tiles

    # ------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    # ------------------------------

    # Within each k-tile, vectorize the reduction over k. The loop body
    # performs independent multiply-adds A[i,k]*A[j,k] (or A[i,k]*A[i,k]),
    # so it is SIMD-friendly. The compiler can implement:
    #   - vector loads from row-major A[i,*] and A[j,*],
    #   - fused multiply-adds accumulating into scalar temporaries.
    vectorize(k, V)

    # Unroll the inner k loop by a small factor to reduce loop overhead and
    # expose more Instructions Per Cycle (IPC). This works together with
    # vectorization; the compiler can group several SIMD vectors per unrolled
    # iteration.
    unroll(k, 4)

    # ------------------------------
    # Parallelization notes
    # ------------------------------

    # The outer dimension i is kept sequential (no parallelize(i)) because
    # every row i depends on all previous rows j < i through A[j,*] and A[j,j].
    # Similarly, j is sequential within each i. Parallelism is thus mainly
    # vector-level (SIMD) and not across threads inside this kernel without
    # switching to a different (e.g., blocked/right-looking) Cholesky algorithm.
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-03 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)            # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)            # column index (only j <= i is updated)
    k: dim in [0, N)            # reduction index for inner products

data:
    # A holds on input a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # On output, its lower triangle (including diagonal) stores the
    # Cholesky factor L such that A_in ≈ L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major

    # Extra 1D buffer storing 1 / A[i, i] after each diagonal is computed.
    # This lets us replace expensive divisions by cheaper multiplications.
    inv_diag[i]: out DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i           # Contiguous 1D layout

parameters:
    N: int                         # problem size (matrix is N x N)

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen to match cache/SIMD of target):
    BJ: int                        # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    BK: int                        # tile size for k (e.g., 64)
    VEC: int                       # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double, 8 for float)
    UNROLL_K: int                  # unroll factor for k (e.g., 4)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky; i and j are explicitly sequential
    # because rows and columns are mutually dependent.
    ROW_FACTOR:
        for i in seq([0, N)):                 # i must be sequential
            # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns 0..i-1.
            OFFDIAG_ROW:
                for j in seq([0, i)):         # j must be sequential within the row
                    # L(i,j) = ( A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) * L(j,k) ) / L(j,j)
                    # We use inv_diag[j] so that division is turned into a multiply.
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j),
                                 A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) * inv_diag[j]

            # Diagonal element in row i:
            DIAG_ROW:
                # L(i,i) = sqrt( A(i,i) - sum_{k<i} L(i,k)^2 )
                A[i, i] =
                    SQRT_FUN( A[i, i]
                              - sum(k in [0, i),
                                     A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

                # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
                # Future off-diagonal updates with column j = i use inv_diag[i].
                inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

optimization:
    # The outer row loop i is left as the outermost and strictly sequential;
    # all true loop-carried dependences go through i.
    hoist(i)

    # There are strong dependences along j within a row (each A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for k<j),
    # so we keep j sequential but tile it for locality.
    block(j, J, BJ)
    # After tiling, iterations are over:
    #   J in [0, ceil(N / BJ)), j_inner in [0, BJ)
    # with the guard j = J*BJ + j_inner < i enforced by the triangular domain.

    # Tile the k reductions (dot products) that appear in both off-diagonal and diagonal
    # updates to improve cache reuse and to create a long inner loop amenable to SIMD.
    block(k, K, BK)

    # Vectorize the innermost k dimension in the reductions. This maps naturally to
    # AVX/AVX-512 on x64 by choosing VEC to match the hardware SIMD width in elements.
    vectorize(k, VEC)

    # Unroll the k loop inside each vector chunk to reduce control overhead and
    # expose more instruction-level parallelism within each core.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # The computation explicitly uses inv_diag[i] instead of performing
    #   A[i, j] /= A[j, j]
    # for every off-diagonal entry. This implements:
    #   1) DIAG_ROW:    inv_diag[j] = 1.0 / A[j, j]    # one division per row
    #   2) OFFDIAG_ROW: A[i, j] *= inv_diag[j]         # many cheap multiplies
    # Thus the number of expensive divisions drops from O(N^2) to O(N),
    # at the cost of an extra O(N) buffer (well below 50% extra memory vs. A).

    # Coarse-grain parallelism across rows or columns is not legal due to
    # the strict data dependences along i and j. If a parallel reduction
    # primitive is available and N is very large, an implementation may
    # optionally parallelize across K (the k-tiles) inside each sum()
    # while respecting reduction semantics; this is not mandated here.
    # Example (optional, not required by default):
    # parallelize(K)
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-04 ---
domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, lower-triangular part is meaningful.
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index, will be used with j < i
    k: dim in [0, N)      # inner-product / reduction index

data:
    # A holds the input symmetric positive definite matrix and is overwritten
    # in-place with its Cholesky factor L (stored in the lower triangle).
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major storage

    # Temporary buffer: reciprocal of diagonal entries, used to replace
    # O(N^2) divisions by multiplications and only incur O(N) divisions.
    inv_diag[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j         # 1 / A[j, j] after row j is completed
                                                    # size O(N), << 50% extra memory

parameters:
    N: int                  # problem size

    # Tuning parameters for the k-dimension (reduction dimension).
    TK: int                 # tile size for k (e.g., 32–128, tuned for L1 cache)
    VEC_K: int              # vector width in k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on SIMD width)
    UNR_K: int              # unroll factor for innermost k loop (e.g., 2–4)

computation:
    # Optional: initialize inv_diag (not strictly needed for correctness, but explicit).
    INIT_INV_DIAG:
      for j in [0, N):
        inv_diag[j] = 0

    # Main in-place left-looking Cholesky factorization:
    # for each row i, we:
    #  1. compute off-diagonal entries A[i, j] for j < i,
    #  2. compute the diagonal entry A[i, i],
    #  3. store its reciprocal in inv_diag[i] for later rows.

    for i in seq(0, N):

        # ----- Off-diagonal entries in row i: columns 0..i-1 -----
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # Dot product of rows i and j up to column j-1:
                #   dot_ij = sum_{k = 0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]:
                  dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # Solve for A[i, j]:
                # Original code:
                #   for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
                #   A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
                #
                # Equivalent mathematically:
                #   A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                #
                # Here we precompute inv_diag[j] = 1 / A[j, j] once, and use:
                OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]:
                  A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) * inv_diag[j]

        # ----- Diagonal entry in row i -----
        # Compute:
        #   diag_correction = sum_{k = 0}^{i-1} A[i, k]^2
        # and then:
        #   A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - diag_correction)
        DIAG_DOT[i]:
          diag_correction = sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          A[i, i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i, i] - diag_correction)

        # Precompute 1 / A[i, i] for reuse in subsequent rows (i' > i).
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          inv_diag[i] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # Naming for clarity:
    #   OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j], OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
    #   DIAG_DOT[i], DIAG_UPDATE[i], INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]
    #   "row(i)" := all operations for this i

    # 1. Row-ordering: row i must complete before any later row that uses its data.
    #    In particular, to compute OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j], row j must be fully done.
    for i in [1, N):
        row(i - 1) -> row(i)

    # 2. Within a row, all OFFDIAG_* at (i, j) depend on the diagonal of row j,
    #    because they require A[j, j] (via inv_diag[j]) and A[j, k] for k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]

    # 3. Diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonal entries in that row.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_DOT[i]
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 4. INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i] depends on the finalized diagonal.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_UPDATE[i] -> INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 5. There are no cross-iteration dependencies inside the k-dimension reductions:
    #    OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j] and DIAG_DOT[i] each reduce into a private scalar, so
    #    iterations in k are independent modulo the reduction.

optimization:
    # 1. Arithmetic optimizations
    #    - Use explicit scalar reductions (dot_ij, diag_correction) instead of
    #      repeatedly updating A[i, j] or A[i, i] inside the k-loop.
    #    - Introduce inv_diag[j] so that:
    #         * we do only N divisions (once per diagonal) in INV_DIAG_UPDATE,
    #         * instead of O(N^2) divisions in OFFDIAG_UPDATE.
    #      The replaced operations are multiplications, which are much cheaper.

    # 2. Blocking of the reduction dimension k
    #    Apply tiling to k in all reductions (OFFDIAG_DOT and DIAG_DOT) so that
    #    each tile of A[i, k] and A[j, k] fits in L1 cache and is reused efficiently.
    #
    #    Conceptually:
    #      for k in [0, j)   ->   for K in [0, ceil(j / TK)):
    #                               for kk in [K*TK, min((K+1)*TK, j)):
    block(k, kk, TK)

    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling of innermost tiles
    #    The kk-dimension is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), so we vectorize
    #    over kk and unroll slightly to gain instruction-level parallelism.
    vectorize(kk, VEC_K)
    unroll(kk, UNR_K)

    # 4. Parallelization across kk (within a reduction)
    #    Each reduction "sum over k" is purely over reads of A; the only write is
    #    into the private accumulator (dot_ij or diag_correction).

{

  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)

void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,

{
  int i, j, k;

    # In-place Cholesky factorization of symmetric positive-definite A.

    # such that A_original = L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}

		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{

    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++) {

    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		     DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;


#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     //j<i
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
           A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
        }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
     }
     // i==j case
     for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
        A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
     }
     A[i][i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i][i]);
  }
#pragma endscop

}

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    j: dim in [0, N)            # column index (only j <= i is updated)
    k: dim in [0, N)            # reduction index for inner products

data:
    # A holds on input a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # On output, its lower triangle (including diagonal) stores the
    # Cholesky factor L such that A_in ≈ L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major

    # Extra 1D buffer storing 1 / A[i, i] after each diagonal is computed.
    # This lets us replace expensive divisions by cheaper multiplications.
    inv_diag[i]: out DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i           # Contiguous 1D layout

parameters:
    N: int                         # problem size (matrix is N x N)

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen to match cache/SIMD of target):
    BJ: int                        # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    BK: int                        # tile size for k (e.g., 64)
    VEC: int                       # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double, 8 for float)
    UNROLL_K: int                  # unroll factor for k (e.g., 4)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky; i and j are explicitly sequential
    # because rows and columns are mutually dependent.
    ROW_FACTOR:
        for i in seq([0, N)):                 # i must be sequential
            # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns 0..i-1.
            OFFDIAG_ROW:
                for j in seq([0, i)):         # j must be sequential within the row
                    # L(i,j) = ( A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) * L(j,k) ) / L(j,j)
                    # We use inv_diag[j] so that division is turned into a multiply.
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j),
                                 A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) * inv_diag[j]

            # Diagonal element in row i:
            DIAG_ROW:
                # L(i,i) = sqrt( A(i,i) - sum_{k<i} L(i,k)^2 )
                A[i, i] =
                    SQRT_FUN( A[i, i]
                              - sum(k in [0, i),
                                     A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

                # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
                # Future off-diagonal updates with column j = i use inv_diag[i].
                inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

optimization:
    # The outer row loop i is left as the outermost and strictly sequential;
    # all true loop-carried dependences go through i.
    hoist(i)

    # There are strong dependences along j within a row (each A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for k<j),
    # so we keep j sequential but tile it for locality.
    block(j, J, BJ)
    # After tiling, iterations are over:
    #   J in [0, ceil(N / BJ)), j_inner in [0, BJ)
    # with the guard j = J*BJ + j_inner < i enforced by the triangular domain.

    # Tile the k reductions (dot products) that appear in both off-diagonal and diagonal
    # updates to improve cache reuse and to create a long inner loop amenable to SIMD.
    block(k, K, BK)

    # Vectorize the innermost k dimension in the reductions. This maps naturally to
    # AVX/AVX-512 on x64 by choosing VEC to match the hardware SIMD width in elements.
    vectorize(k, VEC)

    # Unroll the k loop inside each vector chunk to reduce control overhead and
    # expose more instruction-level parallelism within each core.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # The computation explicitly uses inv_diag[i] instead of performing
    #   A[i, j] /= A[j, j]
    # for every off-diagonal entry. This implements:
    #   1) DIAG_ROW:    inv_diag[j] = 1.0 / A[j, j]    # one division per row
    #   2) OFFDIAG_ROW: A[i, j] *= inv_diag[j]         # many cheap multiplies
    # Thus the number of expensive divisions drops from O(N^2) to O(N),
    # at the cost of an extra O(N) buffer (well below 50% extra memory vs. A).

    # Coarse-grain parallelism across rows or columns is not legal due to
    # the strict data dependences along i and j. If a parallel reduction
    # primitive is available and N is very large, an implementation may
    # optionally parallelize across K (the k-tiles) inside each sum()
    # while respecting reduction semantics; this is not mandated here.
    # Example (optional, not required by default):
    # parallelize(K)
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-03 ---

domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, lower-triangular part is meaningful.
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index, will be used with j < i
    k: dim in [0, N)      # inner-product / reduction index

data:
    # A holds the input symmetric positive definite matrix and is overwritten
    # in-place with its Cholesky factor L (stored in the lower triangle).
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major storage

    # Temporary buffer: reciprocal of diagonal entries, used to replace
    # O(N^2) divisions by multiplications and only incur O(N) divisions.
    inv_diag[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j         # 1 / A[j, j] after row j is completed
                                                    # size O(N), << 50% extra memory

parameters:
    N: int                  # problem size

    # Tuning parameters for the k-dimension (reduction dimension).
    TK: int                 # tile size for k (e.g., 32–128, tuned for L1 cache)
    VEC_K: int              # vector width in k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on SIMD width)
    UNR_K: int              # unroll factor for innermost k loop (e.g., 2–4)

computation:
    # Optional: initialize inv_diag (not strictly needed for correctness, but explicit).
    INIT_INV_DIAG:
      for j in [0, N):
        inv_diag[j] = 0

    # Main in-place left-looking Cholesky factorization:
    # for each row i, we:
    #  1. compute off-diagonal entries A[i, j] for j < i,
    #  2. compute the diagonal entry A[i, i],
    #  3. store its reciprocal in inv_diag[i] for later rows.

    for i in seq(0, N):

        # ----- Off-diagonal entries in row i: columns 0..i-1 -----
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # Dot product of rows i and j up to column j-1:
                #   dot_ij = sum_{k = 0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]:
                  dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # Solve for A[i, j]:
                # Original code:
                #   for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
                #   A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
                #
                # Equivalent mathematically:
                #   A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                #
                # Here we precompute inv_diag[j] = 1 / A[j, j] once, and use:
                OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]:
                  A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) * inv_diag[j]

        # ----- Diagonal entry in row i -----
        # Compute:
        #   diag_correction = sum_{k = 0}^{i-1} A[i, k]^2
        # and then:
        #   A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - diag_correction)
        DIAG_DOT[i]:
          diag_correction = sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          A[i, i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i, i] - diag_correction)

        # Precompute 1 / A[i, i] for reuse in subsequent rows (i' > i).
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          inv_diag[i] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # Naming for clarity:
    #   OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j], OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
    #   DIAG_DOT[i], DIAG_UPDATE[i], INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]
    #   "row(i)" := all operations for this i

    # 1. Row-ordering: row i must complete before any later row that uses its data.
    #    In particular, to compute OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j], row j must be fully done.
    for i in [1, N):
        row(i - 1) -> row(i)

    # 2. Within a row, all OFFDIAG_* at (i, j) depend on the diagonal of row j,
    #    because they require A[j, j] (via inv_diag[j]) and A[j, k] for k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]

    # 3. Diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonal entries in that row.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_DOT[i]
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 4. INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i] depends on the finalized diagonal.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_UPDATE[i] -> INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 5. There are no cross-iteration dependencies inside the k-dimension reductions:
    #    OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j] and DIAG_DOT[i] each reduce into a private scalar, so
    #    iterations in k are independent modulo the reduction.

optimization:
    # 1. Arithmetic optimizations
    #    - Use explicit scalar reductions (dot_ij, diag_correction) instead of
    #      repeatedly updating A[i, j] or A[i, i] inside the k-loop.
    #    - Introduce inv_diag[j] so that:
    #         * we do only N divisions (once per diagonal) in INV_DIAG_UPDATE,
    #         * instead of O(N^2) divisions in OFFDIAG_UPDATE.
    #      The replaced operations are multiplications, which are much cheaper.

    # 2. Blocking of the reduction dimension k
    #    Apply tiling to k in all reductions (OFFDIAG_DOT and DIAG_DOT) so that
    #    each tile of A[i, k] and A[j, k] fits in L1 cache and is reused efficiently.
    #
    #    Conceptually:
    #      for k in [0, j)   ->   for K in [0, ceil(j / TK)):
    #                               for kk in [K*TK, min((K+1)*TK, j)):
    block(k, kk, TK)

    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling of innermost tiles
    #    The kk-dimension is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), so we vectorize
    #    over kk and unroll slightly to gain instruction-level parallelism.
    vectorize(kk, VEC_K)
    unroll(kk, UNR_K)

    # 4. Parallelization across kk (within a reduction)
    #    Each reduction "sum over k" is purely over reads of A; the only write is
    #    into the private accumulator (dot_ij or diag_correction).
    #    We can parallelize tiles of kk using a reduction (tree sum) without
    #    violating dependencies in i or j.
    parallelize(kk)

    # 5. Keep i and j strictly sequential
    #    Outer dimensions i and j are *not* parallelized or interchanged because:
    #      - off-diagonal A[i, j] uses previously computed entries A[i, k] (k < j)
    #        and the fully computed row j,
    #      - diagonal A[i, i] depends on all off-diagonals in the same row,
    #      - row i depends on all rows < i.
    #    Respecting these dependencies preserves the original left-looking Cholesky
    #    factorization order and numerical behavior.

# Optimized model for cholesky.c (lower‑triangular Cholesky factorization)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)         # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)         # column index (only j <= i is used)
    k: dim in [0, N)         # reduction index

data:
    # Dense N x N matrix, row-major. Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is used.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Auxiliary 1D array storing 1 / A[i, i] after row i is factored.
    # This removes repeated divisions inside the main kernel.
    inv_diag[i]: aux DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix dimension
    BI: int   # block size for i-tiling (tunable; e.g., 64)
    VF: int   # SIMD width for vectorization of reductions (e.g., 4 or 8)
    UK: int   # unroll factor for k (multiple of VF; e.g., 4 * VF)

computation:
    # In-place Cholesky factorization of symmetric positive-definite A.
    # On exit, A[i, j] for j <= i contains the lower-triangular factor L
    # such that A_original = L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.

    for i in seq(0, N):                # 0 <= i < N, must be sequential
        # Off-diagonal entries in row i: L[i, j] for 0 <= j < i.
        # seq(0, i) denotes the half-open interval 0 <= j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):            # loop-carried deps: j is sequential
            S_off(i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j),
                            A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    * inv_diag[j]      # multiply by precomputed 1 / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal entry in row i: L[i, i].
        S_diag(i):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(              # matches SQRT_FUN used in the C code
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i),
                          A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

        # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for use in later rows.
        S_inv(i):
            inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. Each off-diagonal element L[i, j] depends on:
    #    - the diagonal factor (via its reciprocal) from row j
    #    - all earlier off-diagonals in the same row i
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_inv(j) -> S_off(i, j)        # need inv_diag[j] before using it
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i), k in [0, j):
        S_off(i, k) -> S_off(i, j)     # A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for k < j

    # 2. The diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonals in that row.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_off(i, j) -> S_diag(i)

    # 3. inv_diag[i] depends on the final value of the diagonal A[i, i].
    for i in [0, N):
        S_diag(i) -> S_inv(i)

optimization:
    # Arithmetic optimization:
    # - The auxiliary array inv_diag[i] hoists one division per (i, j) pair
    #   out of the inner loops. Each off-diagonal update now performs a
    #   multiply instead of a divide, which is substantially cheaper on x64.

    # Cache / locality optimization:
    # - Tile the outer i-loop so that the working set of a block of rows
    #   (their off-diagonals and partial diagonals) fits better into cache.
    block(i, I, BI)          # I: tile index over rows, BI: tunable tile size
    hoist(I)                 # place the tile loop as outermost around i

    # Vectorization and ILP:
    # - The k-dimension in both reductions is free of cross-iteration
    #   dependencies except for the scalar reduction variable, so it can be
    #   efficiently SIMD-vectorized and unrolled.
    vectorize(k, VF)         # use SIMD width VF along k
    unroll(k, UK)            # unroll the k-loop by factor UK (multiple of VF)

    # Parallelism:
    # - Due to explicit dependencies between rows (i dimension) and columns
    #   (j dimension), i and j must remain sequential. Parallelism is
    #   therefore exploited only via vectorization of k.
    #   No parallelize(i) or parallelize(j) is legal here.

    # Triangular structure:
    # - Only the lower triangle of A is live. No computation or stores touch
    #   elements with j > i; this is enforced by the bounds j < i in S_off
    #   and by using only A[i, k] with k < i in S_diag.

#include <stdio.h>

#include <string.h>
#include <math.h>

/* Include polybench common header. */
#include <polybench.h>

/* Include benchmark-specific header. */
#include "cholesky.h"


/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++) {
    if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		     DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;


#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     //j<i
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
           A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
        }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
     }
     // i==j case
     for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
        A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
     }
     A[i][i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i][i]);
  }
#pragma endscop

}


int main(int argc, char** argv)
{
  /* Retrieve problem size. */
  int n = N;

  /* Variable declaration/allocation. */
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  /* Initialize array(s). */
  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Start timer. */
  polybench_start_instruments;

  /* Run kernel. */
  kernel_cholesky (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  /* Stop and print timer. */
  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  /* Prevent dead-code elimination. All live-out data must be printed
     by the function call in argument. */
  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  /* Be clean. */
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A is an N×N matrix stored in row-major layout.
    # Only the lower-triangular part (j <= i) is used/updated by the kernel.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    # Tunable constants for performance; values should be chosen based on cache sizes and SIMD width.
    T_I: int  # tile size for i (e.g., 64)
    T_J: int  # tile size for j within each row (e.g., 64)
    T_K: int  # tile size for k in reductions (e.g., 64)
    V_K: int  # SIMD vector width along k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky factorization: A becomes its own lower-triangular factor L.
    for i in seq(0, N):
        # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # dot_ij = Σ_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                DOT_OFF:
                    dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # A[i, j] ← (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                OFF:
                    A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal element in row i.
        # dot_ii = Σ_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[i, k]
        DOT_DIAG:
            dot_ii = sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        # A[i, i] ← sqrt(A[i, i] - dot_ii)
        # SQRT_FUN in the original code is modeled as the standard sqrt for DATA_TYPE.
        DIAG:
            A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - dot_ii)

dependencies:
    # Within a fixed row i, the off-diagonal elements A[i, j] must be computed left-to-right
    # because A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for all k < j that were produced by earlier OFF updates.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):
        OFF(i, j-1) -> OFF(i, j)

    # The diagonal element A[i, i] depends on all off-diagonal elements of row i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        OFF(i, j) -> DIAG(i)

    # The outer loop over i is strictly sequential (left-looking factorization):
    # row i depends on all rows 0..i-1 having been fully factorized.
    # This is already enforced by "for i in seq(0, N)" but is stated explicitly here.
    for i in [1, N):
        DIAG(i-1) -> OFF(i, 0)

optimization:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Blocking / tiling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block the outer i-loop to improve temporal locality for rows of A.
    # This preserves the sequential order of i within each tile, so the
    # Cholesky row-to-row dependencies remain intact.
    block(i, I, T_I)

    # Block the j-loop within each row i. Although j’s upper bound depends
    # on i (j < i), the blocking is applied over the full [0, N) range,
    # with the j < i condition still guarding the triangular region.
    # This improves reuse when processing bands of the lower triangle.
    block(j, J, T_J)

    # Block the k-dimension of the dot products so that each k-tile fits
    # into L1/L2 cache. This reduces cache misses when streaming A[i, k]
    # and A[j, k] in the reductions.
    block(k, K, T_K)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost k-iteration in both dot products:
    #   dot_ij = Σ A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #   dot_ii = Σ A[i, k] * A[i, k]
    # Mapping these to SIMD FMA instructions significantly increases throughput.
    vectorize(k, V_K)

    # Additional unrolling of k increases ILP (instruction-level parallelism)
    # and helps hide the latency of loads and floating-point operations.
    unroll(k, 4)

    # Parallelism
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The outer i-loop and the j-loop inside a row cannot be parallelized
    # due to true data dependencies (each row depends on all previous rows,
    # and each A[i, j] depends on A[i, k] for k < j).
    #
    # However, the reductions over k for a fixed (i, j) are mathematically
    # associative, so they can be parallelized across k-tiles K. Each
    # thread computes a partial sum over a subset of K and partial sums
    # are combined at the end of the reduction.
    parallelize(K)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar replacement / register promotion (conceptual)
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The compiler is encouraged to keep frequently used scalar values,
    # such as A[j, j] and the running sums dot_ij, dot_ii, in registers.
    # This is implied by the formulation using scalar temporaries (dot_ij,
    # dot_ii) and the absence of aliasing, and does not require an
    # explicit directive in this model.

    # written in one assignment so that the sum is accumulated in registers
    # instead of repeatedly updating A[i,j] in memory.

        for i in seq([0, N)):

                    ( A[i, j]

        for i in seq([0, N)):

    # A[j,k] for k < j (used in the dot product).

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):

    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky; i and j are explicitly sequential
    # because rows and columns are mutually dependent.

        for i in seq([0, N)):                 # i must be sequential
            # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns 0..i-1.
            OFFDIAG_ROW:
                for j in seq([0, i)):         # j must be sequential within the row
                    # L(i,j) = ( A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) * L(j,k) ) / L(j,j)
                    # We use inv_diag[j] so that division is turned into a multiply.
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j),
                                 A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) * inv_diag[j]

            # Diagonal element in row i:
            DIAG_ROW:
                # L(i,i) = sqrt( A(i,i) - sum_{k<i} L(i,k)^2 )
                A[i, i] =
                    SQRT_FUN( A[i, i]
                              - sum(k in [0, i),
                                     A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

                # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
                # Future off-diagonal updates with column j = i use inv_diag[i].

    # The outer row loop i is left as the outermost and strictly sequential;

    #  3. store its reciprocal in inv_diag[i] for later rows.

    k: dim in [0, N)         # reduction index

    UK: int   # unroll factor for k (multiple of VF; e.g., 4 * VF)

    # In-place Cholesky factorization of symmetric positive-definite A.
    # On exit, A[i, j] for j <= i contains the lower-triangular factor L
    # such that A_original = L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.

    for i in seq(0, N):                # 0 <= i < N, must be sequential

        # seq(0, i) denotes the half-open interval 0 <= j < i.

                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j),
                            A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    * inv_diag[j]      # multiply by precomputed 1 / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal entry in row i: L[i, i].
        S_diag(i):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(              # matches SQRT_FUN used in the C code
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i),
                          A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

        S_inv(i):
            inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

    # 1. Each off-diagonal element L[i, j] depends on:
    #    - the diagonal factor (via its reciprocal) from row j
    #    - all earlier off-diagonals in the same row i

    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i), k in [0, j):

    for i in [0, N):

/* Array initialization. */
static
void init_array(int n,
		DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j;

  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    {
      for (j = 0; j <= i; j++)
	A[i][j] = (DATA_TYPE)(-j % n) / n + 1;
      for (j = i+1; j < n; j++) {
	A[i][j] = 0;
      }
      A[i][i] = 1;
    }

  /* Make the matrix positive semi-definite. */
  int r,s,t;
  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(B, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);
  for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
    for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
      (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] = 0;
  for (t = 0; t < n; ++t)
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	(POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s] += A[r][t] * A[s][t];
    for (r = 0; r < n; ++r)
      for (s = 0; s < n; ++s)
	A[r][s] = (POLYBENCH_ARRAY(B))[r][s];
  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(B);

}


/* DCE code. Must scan the entire live-out data.
   Can be used also to check the correctness of the output. */
static
void print_array(int n,
		 DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))

{
  int i, j;

  POLYBENCH_DUMP_START;
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_BEGIN("A");
  for (i = 0; i < n; i++)
    for (j = 0; j <= i; j++) {
    if ((i * n + j) % 20 == 0) fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, "\n");
    fprintf (POLYBENCH_DUMP_TARGET, DATA_PRINTF_MODIFIER, A[i][j]);
  }
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_END("A");
  POLYBENCH_DUMP_FINISH;
}


/* Main computational kernel. The whole function will be timed,
   including the call and return. */
static
void kernel_cholesky[[gnu::flatten, gnu::noinline]](int n,
		     DATA_TYPE POLYBENCH_2D(A,N,N,n,n))
{
  int i, j, k;


#pragma scop
  for (i = 0; i < _PB_N; i++) {
     //j<i
     for (j = 0; j < i; j++) {
        for (k = 0; k < j; k++) {
           A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
        }
        A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
     }
     // i==j case
     for (k = 0; k < i; k++) {
        A[i][i] -= A[i][k] * A[i][k];
     }
     A[i][i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i][i]);
  }
#pragma endscop

}

  POLYBENCH_2D_ARRAY_DECL(A, DATA_TYPE, N, N, n, n);

  init_array (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  polybench_start_instruments;

  kernel_cholesky (n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A));

  polybench_stop_instruments;
  polybench_print_instruments;

  polybench_prevent_dce(print_array(n, POLYBENCH_ARRAY(A)));

  POLYBENCH_FREE_ARRAY(A);

  return 0;
}

    # Full logical domain; triangular structure is expressed in the computation via j < i, k < j.
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # A is an N×N matrix stored in row-major layout.
    # Only the lower-triangular part (j <= i) is used/updated by the kernel.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    # Tunable constants for performance; values should be chosen based on cache sizes and SIMD width.
    T_I: int  # tile size for i (e.g., 64)
    T_J: int  # tile size for j within each row (e.g., 64)
    T_K: int  # tile size for k in reductions (e.g., 64)
    V_K: int  # SIMD vector width along k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on DATA_TYPE and ISA)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky factorization: A becomes its own lower-triangular factor L.
    for i in seq(0, N):
        # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # dot_ij = Σ_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                DOT_OFF:
                    dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # A[i, j] ← (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                OFF:
                    A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal element in row i.
        # dot_ii = Σ_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i, k] * A[i, k]
        DOT_DIAG:
            dot_ii = sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        # A[i, i] ← sqrt(A[i, i] - dot_ii)
        # SQRT_FUN in the original code is modeled as the standard sqrt for DATA_TYPE.
        DIAG:
            A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - dot_ii)

dependencies:
    # Within a fixed row i, the off-diagonal elements A[i, j] must be computed left-to-right
    # because A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for all k < j that were produced by earlier OFF updates.
    for i in [0, N), j in [1, i):
        OFF(i, j-1) -> OFF(i, j)

    # The diagonal element A[i, i] depends on all off-diagonal elements of row i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        OFF(i, j) -> DIAG(i)

    # The outer loop over i is strictly sequential (left-looking factorization):
    # row i depends on all rows 0..i-1 having been fully factorized.
    # This is already enforced by "for i in seq(0, N)" but is stated explicitly here.
    for i in [1, N):
        DIAG(i-1) -> OFF(i, 0)

optimization:
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Blocking / tiling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Block the outer i-loop to improve temporal locality for rows of A.
    # This preserves the sequential order of i within each tile, so the
    # Cholesky row-to-row dependencies remain intact.
    block(i, I, T_I)

    # Block the j-loop within each row i. Although j’s upper bound depends
    # on i (j < i), the blocking is applied over the full [0, N) range,
    # with the j < i condition still guarding the triangular region.
    # This improves reuse when processing bands of the lower triangle.
    block(j, J, T_J)

    # Block the k-dimension of the dot products so that each k-tile fits
    # into L1/L2 cache. This reduces cache misses when streaming A[i, k]
    # and A[j, k] in the reductions.
    block(k, K, T_K)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Vectorize the innermost k-iteration in both dot products:
    #   dot_ij = Σ A[i, k] * A[j, k]
    #   dot_ii = Σ A[i, k] * A[i, k]
    # Mapping these to SIMD FMA instructions significantly increases throughput.
    vectorize(k, V_K)

    # Additional unrolling of k increases ILP (instruction-level parallelism)
    # and helps hide the latency of loads and floating-point operations.
    unroll(k, 4)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Parallelism
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The outer i-loop and the j-loop inside a row cannot be parallelized
    # due to true data dependencies (each row depends on all previous rows,
    # and each A[i, j] depends on A[i, k] for k < j).
    #
    # However, the reductions over k for a fixed (i, j) are mathematically
    # associative, so they can be parallelized across k-tiles K. Each
    # thread computes a partial sum over a subset of K and partial sums
    # are combined at the end of the reduction.
    parallelize(K)

    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Scalar replacement / register promotion (conceptual)
    #--------------------------------------------------------------------
    # The compiler is encouraged to keep frequently used scalar values,
    # such as A[j, j] and the running sums dot_ij, dot_ii, in registers.
    # This is implied by the formulation using scalar temporaries (dot_ij,
    # dot_ii) and the absence of aliasing, and does not require an
    # explicit directive in this model.
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-01 ---

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-02 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)
    j: dim in [0, N)
    k: dim in [0, N)

data:
    # Full N×N matrix stored row-major; only the lower triangle (j ≤ i) is used.
    # On input: A is symmetric positive definite.
    # On output: A holds the Cholesky factor L (lower-triangular) such that A ≈ L · Lᵀ.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j  # row-major

parameters:
    N: int  # matrix dimension

    # Cache / SIMD tuning parameters
    TI: int  # tile size for i (e.g., 32)
    TJ: int  # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    TK: int  # tile size for k-reductions (e.g., 64)
    V:  int  # SIMD width for vectorization over k (e.g., 8 for AVX-512 double)

computation:
    # Off-diagonal entries: for each row i, columns j < i.
    # This expresses the left-looking Cholesky update:
    #   A[i,j] = (A[i,j] - ∑_{k=0}^{j-1} A[i,k] * A[j,k]) / A[j,j]
    # written in one assignment so that the sum is accumulated in registers
    # instead of repeatedly updating A[i,j] in memory.
    OFFDIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            for j in seq([0, i)):   # sequential in j: A[i,j] depends on A[i,0..j-1]
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j)) (A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    / A[j, j]

    # Diagonal entries:
    #   A[i,i] = sqrt( A[i,i] - ∑_{k=0}^{i-1} A[i,k]^2 )
    # again with the reduction written explicitly.
    DIAG:
        for i in seq([0, N)):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i)) (A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

dependencies:
    # Within a fixed row i, off-diagonal elements must be computed in increasing j,
    # because A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for all k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j1 in [0, N), j2 in [0, N):
        if (j1 < j2) and (j2 < i):
            OFFDIAG(i, j1) -> OFFDIAG(i, j2)

    # Each off-diagonal element A[i,j] depends on the entire row j (0..j) being
    # already factorized, in particular on A[j,j] (for the division) and
    # A[j,k] for k < j (used in the dot product).
    # This is enforced by depending on DIAG(j), which in turn depends on all
    # OFFDIAG(j, k) with k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        if j < i:
            DIAG(j) -> OFFDIAG(i, j)

    # The diagonal element A[i,i] depends on all off-diagonal elements in row i,
    # since its reduction uses A[i,k] for k < i.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, N):
        if j < i:
            OFFDIAG(i, j) -> DIAG(i)

optimization:
    # ------------------------------
    # Loop blocking (tiling)
    # ------------------------------

    # Block the outer i and j dimensions. This restructures the triangular
    # iteration into tiles but preserves the original lexicographic order
    # (and thus dependencies). Many tiles will be partially filled because
    # of the j < i constraint, but data locality improves: elements of nearby
    # rows/columns live in cache together.
    block(i, I, TI)
    block(j, J, TJ)
    hoist(I)   # I is the outermost loop
    hoist(J)   # J is just inside I, before the scalar i,j loops

    # Block the reduction dimension k for both reductions. This lets us:
    #   - operate on TK-sized chunks of rows A[i,*] and A[j,*],
    #   - keep those chunks in cache,
    #   - vectorize efficiently across k.
    # The transformation logically turns
    #   sum(k in [0, bound)) ...
    # into nested sums over tiles Kb and intra-tile k, handling short
    # last tiles when bound is not multiple of TK.
    block(k, Kb, TK)
    hoist(Kb)  # Kb is hoisted outside the innermost loops to reuse tiles

    # ------------------------------
    # Vectorization and unrolling
    # ------------------------------

    # Within each k-tile, vectorize the reduction over k. The loop body
    # performs independent multiply-adds A[i,k]*A[j,k] (or A[i,k]*A[i,k]),
    # so it is SIMD-friendly. The compiler can implement:
    #   - vector loads from row-major A[i,*] and A[j,*],
    #   - fused multiply-adds accumulating into scalar temporaries.
    vectorize(k, V)

    # Unroll the inner k loop by a small factor to reduce loop overhead and
    # expose more Instructions Per Cycle (IPC). This works together with
    # vectorization; the compiler can group several SIMD vectors per unrolled
    # iteration.
    unroll(k, 4)

    # ------------------------------
    # Parallelization notes
    # ------------------------------

    # The outer dimension i is kept sequential (no parallelize(i)) because
    # every row i depends on all previous rows j < i through A[j,*] and A[j,j].
    # Similarly, j is sequential within each i. Parallelism is thus mainly
    # vector-level (SIMD) and not across threads inside this kernel without
    # switching to a different (e.g., blocked/right-looking) Cholesky algorithm.
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-02 ---

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-03 ---
domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)            # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)            # column index (only j <= i is updated)
    k: dim in [0, N)            # reduction index for inner products

data:
    # A holds on input a symmetric positive semi-definite matrix.
    # On output, its lower triangle (including diagonal) stores the
    # Cholesky factor L such that A_in ≈ L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # Row-major

    # Extra 1D buffer storing 1 / A[i, i] after each diagonal is computed.
    # This lets us replace expensive divisions by cheaper multiplications.
    inv_diag[i]: out DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i           # Contiguous 1D layout

parameters:
    N: int                         # problem size (matrix is N x N)

    # Tunable optimization parameters (chosen to match cache/SIMD of target):
    BJ: int                        # tile size for j (e.g., 32)
    BK: int                        # tile size for k (e.g., 64)
    VEC: int                       # SIMD width in elements (e.g., 4 for double, 8 for float)
    UNROLL_K: int                  # unroll factor for k (e.g., 4)

computation:
    # Left-looking in-place Cholesky; i and j are explicitly sequential
    # because rows and columns are mutually dependent.
    ROW_FACTOR:
        for i in seq([0, N)):                 # i must be sequential
            # Off-diagonal elements in row i: columns 0..i-1.
            OFFDIAG_ROW:
                for j in seq([0, i)):         # j must be sequential within the row
                    # L(i,j) = ( A(i,j) - sum_{k<j} L(i,k) * L(j,k) ) / L(j,j)
                    # We use inv_diag[j] so that division is turned into a multiply.
                    A[i, j] =
                        ( A[i, j]
                          - sum(k in [0, j),
                                 A[i, k] * A[j, k]) ) * inv_diag[j]

            # Diagonal element in row i:
            DIAG_ROW:
                # L(i,i) = sqrt( A(i,i) - sum_{k<i} L(i,k)^2 )
                A[i, i] =
                    SQRT_FUN( A[i, i]
                              - sum(k in [0, i),
                                     A[i, k] * A[i, k]) )

                # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for later rows.
                # Future off-diagonal updates with column j = i use inv_diag[i].
                inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

optimization:
    # The outer row loop i is left as the outermost and strictly sequential;
    # all true loop-carried dependences go through i.
    hoist(i)

    # There are strong dependences along j within a row (each A[i,j] uses A[i,k] for k<j),
    # so we keep j sequential but tile it for locality.
    block(j, J, BJ)
    # After tiling, iterations are over:
    #   J in [0, ceil(N / BJ)), j_inner in [0, BJ)
    # with the guard j = J*BJ + j_inner < i enforced by the triangular domain.

    # Tile the k reductions (dot products) that appear in both off-diagonal and diagonal
    # updates to improve cache reuse and to create a long inner loop amenable to SIMD.
    block(k, K, BK)

    # Vectorize the innermost k dimension in the reductions. This maps naturally to
    # AVX/AVX-512 on x64 by choosing VEC to match the hardware SIMD width in elements.
    vectorize(k, VEC)

    # Unroll the k loop inside each vector chunk to reduce control overhead and
    # expose more instruction-level parallelism within each core.
    unroll(k, UNROLL_K)

    # The computation explicitly uses inv_diag[i] instead of performing
    #   A[i, j] /= A[j, j]
    # for every off-diagonal entry. This implements:
    #   1) DIAG_ROW:    inv_diag[j] = 1.0 / A[j, j]    # one division per row
    #   2) OFFDIAG_ROW: A[i, j] *= inv_diag[j]         # many cheap multiplies
    # Thus the number of expensive divisions drops from O(N^2) to O(N),
    # at the cost of an extra O(N) buffer (well below 50% extra memory vs. A).

    # Coarse-grain parallelism across rows or columns is not legal due to
    # the strict data dependences along i and j. If a parallel reduction
    # primitive is available and N is very large, an implementation may
    # optionally parallelize across K (the k-tiles) inside each sum()
    # while respecting reduction semantics; this is not mandated here.
    # Example (optional, not required by default):
    # parallelize(K)
--- END OF MODEL: cholesky-03 ---

--- START OF MODEL: cholesky-04 ---
domain:
    # Matrix is N x N, lower-triangular part is meaningful.
    i: dim in [0, N)      # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)      # column index, will be used with j < i
    k: dim in [0, N)      # inner-product / reduction index

data:
    # A holds the input symmetric positive definite matrix and is overwritten
    # in-place with its Cholesky factor L (stored in the lower triangle).
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j   # row-major storage

    # Temporary buffer: reciprocal of diagonal entries, used to replace
    # O(N^2) divisions by multiplications and only incur O(N) divisions.
    inv_diag[j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (j) -> j         # 1 / A[j, j] after row j is completed
                                                    # size O(N), << 50% extra memory

parameters:
    N: int                  # problem size

    # Tuning parameters for the k-dimension (reduction dimension).
    TK: int                 # tile size for k (e.g., 32–128, tuned for L1 cache)
    VEC_K: int              # vector width in k (e.g., 4 or 8 depending on SIMD width)
    UNR_K: int              # unroll factor for innermost k loop (e.g., 2–4)

computation:
    # Optional: initialize inv_diag (not strictly needed for correctness, but explicit).
    INIT_INV_DIAG:
      for j in [0, N):
        inv_diag[j] = 0

    # Main in-place left-looking Cholesky factorization:
    # for each row i, we:
    #  1. compute off-diagonal entries A[i, j] for j < i,
    #  2. compute the diagonal entry A[i, i],
    #  3. store its reciprocal in inv_diag[i] for later rows.

    for i in seq(0, N):

        # ----- Off-diagonal entries in row i: columns 0..i-1 -----
        for j in seq(0, i):
            if j < i:
                # Dot product of rows i and j up to column j-1:
                #   dot_ij = sum_{k = 0}^{j-1} A[i, k] * A[j, k]
                OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]:
                  dot_ij = sum(k in [0, j), A[i, k] * A[j, k])

                # Solve for A[i, j]:
                # Original code:
                #   for (k = 0; k < j; k++) A[i][j] -= A[i][k] * A[j][k];
                #   A[i][j] /= A[j][j];
                #
                # Equivalent mathematically:
                #   A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) / A[j, j]
                #
                # Here we precompute inv_diag[j] = 1 / A[j, j] once, and use:
                OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]:
                  A[i, j] = (A[i, j] - dot_ij) * inv_diag[j]

        # ----- Diagonal entry in row i -----
        # Compute:
        #   diag_correction = sum_{k = 0}^{i-1} A[i, k]^2
        # and then:
        #   A[i, i] = sqrt(A[i, i] - diag_correction)
        DIAG_DOT[i]:
          diag_correction = sum(k in [0, i), A[i, k] * A[i, k])

        DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          A[i, i] = SQRT_FUN(A[i, i] - diag_correction)

        # Precompute 1 / A[i, i] for reuse in subsequent rows (i' > i).
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]:
          inv_diag[i] = (DATA_TYPE)1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # Naming for clarity:
    #   OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j], OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
    #   DIAG_DOT[i], DIAG_UPDATE[i], INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]
    #   "row(i)" := all operations for this i

    # 1. Row-ordering: row i must complete before any later row that uses its data.
    #    In particular, to compute OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j], row j must be fully done.
    for i in [1, N):
        row(i - 1) -> row(i)

    # 2. Within a row, all OFFDIAG_* at (i, j) depend on the diagonal of row j,
    #    because they require A[j, j] (via inv_diag[j]) and A[j, k] for k < j.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j]
        DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]
        INV_DIAG_UPDATE[j] -> OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j]

    # 3. Diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonal entries in that row.
    for i in [0, N):
        for j in [0, i):
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_DOT[i]
            OFFDIAG_UPDATE[i, j] -> DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 4. INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i] depends on the finalized diagonal.
    for i in [0, N):
        DIAG_UPDATE[i] -> INV_DIAG_UPDATE[i]

    # 5. There are no cross-iteration dependencies inside the k-dimension reductions:
    #    OFFDIAG_DOT[i, j] and DIAG_DOT[i] each reduce into a private scalar, so
    #    iterations in k are independent modulo the reduction.

optimization:
    # 1. Arithmetic optimizations
    #    - Use explicit scalar reductions (dot_ij, diag_correction) instead of
    #      repeatedly updating A[i, j] or A[i, i] inside the k-loop.
    #    - Introduce inv_diag[j] so that:
    #         * we do only N divisions (once per diagonal) in INV_DIAG_UPDATE,
    #         * instead of O(N^2) divisions in OFFDIAG_UPDATE.
    #      The replaced operations are multiplications, which are much cheaper.

    # 2. Blocking of the reduction dimension k
    #    Apply tiling to k in all reductions (OFFDIAG_DOT and DIAG_DOT) so that
    #    each tile of A[i, k] and A[j, k] fits in L1 cache and is reused efficiently.
    #
    #    Conceptually:
    #      for k in [0, j)   ->   for K in [0, ceil(j / TK)):
    #                               for kk in [K*TK, min((K+1)*TK, j)):
    block(k, kk, TK)

    # 3. Vectorization and unrolling of innermost tiles
    #    The kk-dimension is contiguous in memory (row-major layout), so we vectorize
    #    over kk and unroll slightly to gain instruction-level parallelism.
    vectorize(kk, VEC_K)
    unroll(kk, UNR_K)

    # 4. Parallelization across kk (within a reduction)
    #    Each reduction "sum over k" is purely over reads of A; the only write is
    #    into the private accumulator (dot_ij or diag_correction).
    #    We can parallelize tiles of kk using a reduction (tree sum) without
    #    violating dependencies in i or j.
    parallelize(kk)

    # 5. Keep i and j strictly sequential
    #    Outer dimensions i and j are *not* parallelized or interchanged because:
    #      - off-diagonal A[i, j] uses previously computed entries A[i, k] (k < j)
    #        and the fully computed row j,
    #      - diagonal A[i, i] depends on all off-diagonals in the same row,
    #      - row i depends on all rows < i.
    #    Respecting these dependencies preserves the original left-looking Cholesky
    #    factorization order and numerical behavior.

# Optimized model for cholesky.c (lower‑triangular Cholesky factorization)

domain:
    i: dim in [0, N)         # row index
    j: dim in [0, N)         # column index (only j <= i is used)
    k: dim in [0, N)         # reduction index

data:
    # Dense N x N matrix, row-major. Only the lower triangle (j <= i) is used.
    A[i, j]: inout DATA_TYPE = (i, j) -> i * N + j

    # Auxiliary 1D array storing 1 / A[i, i] after row i is factored.
    # This removes repeated divisions inside the main kernel.
    inv_diag[i]: aux DATA_TYPE = (i) -> i

parameters:
    N:  int   # matrix dimension
    BI: int   # block size for i-tiling (tunable; e.g., 64)
    VF: int   # SIMD width for vectorization of reductions (e.g., 4 or 8)
    UK: int   # unroll factor for k (multiple of VF; e.g., 4 * VF)

computation:
    # In-place Cholesky factorization of symmetric positive-definite A.
    # On exit, A[i, j] for j <= i contains the lower-triangular factor L
    # such that A_original = L * L^T. The upper triangle is unused.

    for i in seq(0, N):                # 0 <= i < N, must be sequential
        # Off-diagonal entries in row i: L[i, j] for 0 <= j < i.
        # seq(0, i) denotes the half-open interval 0 <= j < i.
        for j in seq(0, i):            # loop-carried deps: j is sequential
            S_off(i, j):
                A[i, j] =
                    ( A[i, j]
                      - sum(k in [0, j),
                            A[i, k] * A[j, k]) )
                    * inv_diag[j]      # multiply by precomputed 1 / A[j, j]

        # Diagonal entry in row i: L[i, i].
        S_diag(i):
            A[i, i] =
                SQRT_FUN(              # matches SQRT_FUN used in the C code
                    A[i, i]
                    - sum(k in [0, i),
                          A[i, k] * A[i, k])
                )

        # Precompute reciprocal of the diagonal for use in later rows.
        S_inv(i):
            inv_diag[i] = 1.0 / A[i, i]

dependencies:
    # 1. Each off-diagonal element L[i, j] depends on:
    #    - the diagonal factor (via its reciprocal) from row j
    #    - all earlier off-diagonals in the same row i
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_inv(j) -> S_off(i, j)        # need inv_diag[j] before using it
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i), k in [0, j):
        S_off(i, k) -> S_off(i, j)     # A[i, j] uses A[i, k] for k < j

    # 2. The diagonal of row i depends on all off-diagonals in that row.
    for i in [0, N), j in [0, i):
        S_off(i, j) -> S_diag(i)

    # 3. inv_diag[i] depends on the final value of the diagonal A[i, i].
    for i in [0, N):
        S_diag(i) -> S_inv(i)

optimization:
    # Arithmetic optimization:
    # - The auxiliary array inv_diag[i] hoists one division per (i, j) pair
    #   out of the inner loops. Each off-diagonal update now performs a
    #   multiply instead of a divide, which is substantially cheaper on x64.

    # Cache / locality optimization:
    # - Tile the outer i-loop so that the working set of a block of rows
    #   (their off-diagonals and partial diagonals) fits better into cache.
    block(i, I, BI)          # I: tile index over rows, BI: tunable tile size
    hoist(I)                 # place the tile loop as outermost around i

    # Vectorization and ILP:
    # - The k-dimension in both reductions is free of cross-iteration
    #   dependencies except for the scalar reduction variable, so it can be
